q: A serving employee reports to his health unit. The Authorised Medical Attendant finds that the required facility is not available in the railway hospital. What is the correct course for treatment outside the railway system?

options.A: Accounts may directly sanction treatment in any hospital on request
options.B: The employee may choose any private hospital and claim full reimbursement as of right
options.C: The case is referred to a government or empanelled hospital through the prescribed medical authority, at the CMD/CMS level as prescribed
options.D: The employee must wait until the facility is created in the railway hospital

q: A railway employee's family member suffers a life-threatening emergency at night and is taken to the nearest private hospital without any referral. A reimbursement claim is later submitted. What must be established for the claim to proceed?

options.A: Nothing further is needed, because any private hospital treatment is reimbursable
options.B: Only the total bill amount needs to be certified by the employee
options.C: The claim proceeds only if the hospital is the costliest in the city
options.D: The emergency must be certified by the treating authority and accepted by the competent railway medical authority, with the claim supported by bills, discharge summary and sanction

q: During pension work, Accounts finds that a pensioner is drawing Fixed Medical Allowance every month and is also regularly availing outdoor treatment at the railway hospital. What does this situation represent?

options.A: A permissible combination, because FMA is payable in addition to OPD treatment
options.B: A permissible combination, because FMA covers indoor treatment only
options.C: The classic double-benefit irregularity: FMA is payable only when the OPD facility is not availed
options.D: An irregularity only if the pensioner also takes indoor treatment

q: An empanelled hospital's bill for a referred case includes extra procedures and a longer stay that go beyond the referral letter, with no medical justification recorded. What should Accounts do?

options.A: Pass the bill in full because the hospital is empanelled
options.B: Reject the entire treatment, including the referred portion
options.C: Pay only the referral-letter amount and ignore the documents
options.D: Not pass the excess mechanically; the bill beyond the referral needs medical justification and approval, checked against the referral letter, package rates and discharge summary

q: A RELHS pensioner wishes to take routine, non-emergency treatment in an empanelled private hospital of his choice, without any referral from the railway medical authority, and expects reimbursement. What is the correct position?

options.A: Treatment in a recognised or empanelled hospital is admissible only in an emergency or on being referred, following the prescribed procedure
options.B: A RELHS pensioner may take treatment anywhere as of right, unlike serving staff
options.C: Reimbursement is automatic if the pensioner produces the UMID card alone
options.D: Reimbursement is automatic if the bill is below the FMA amount

q: Consider the following statements about RELHS joining and subscription: I. Joining RELHS is optional for a retiring employee. II. The one-time contribution is equal to one month's basic pay last drawn. III. The option is exercised at retirement and the subscription is recovered along with the settlement process. IV. The one-time contribution is equal to one month's pension. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.A: I only
options.B: I, II and III only
options.C: II and IV only
options.D: I, II, III and IV

q: Consider the following statements about the UMID card: I. UMID stands for Unique Medical Identification. II. It is issued to serving employees, pensioners and their eligible family members and dependants. III. Each beneficiary has his own unique UMID number. IV. It is issued only to pensioners, and serving employees continue on paper cards. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.A: I only
options.B: I and III only
options.C: I, II and III only
options.D: I, II, III and IV

q: Consider the following statements about Fixed Medical Allowance: I. FMA is paid at Rs 1,000 per month under the 7th CPC dispensation. II. FMA is admissible only to a pensioner who is not availing the outdoor (OPD) treatment facility. III. A pensioner drawing FMA is barred from indoor treatment in a railway hospital. IV. FMA is in lieu of OPD treatment for day-to-day minor ailments. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.A: I and II only
options.B: II and III only
options.C: I, II, III and IV
options.D: I, II and IV only

q: RELHS, the post-retirement health scheme of the Railways, stands for:

options.A: Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme
options.B: Railway Employees Liberalised Health Scheme
options.C: Retired Employees Limited Health Scheme
options.D: Railway Employees Long-term Health Scheme

q: UMID, the medical identity smart card issued to railway beneficiaries, stands for:

options.A: Unique Medical Insurance Card
options.B: Unique Medical Identification
options.C: Universal Medical Identity Document
options.D: Unified Medical Insurance Document

q: The Fixed Medical Allowance payable to an eligible railway pensioner who does not avail the OPD facility is, under the 7th CPC dispensation with effect from 01.07.2017:

options.A: Rs 500 per month
options.B: Rs 1,000 per month
options.C: Rs 2,000 per month
options.D: Rs 300 per month

q: The one-time contribution payable by a retiring railway servant for joining RELHS is equal to:

options.A: One month's pension
options.B: A fixed flat fee prescribed for all levels
options.C: One month's pay plus dearness allowance last drawn
options.D: One month's basic pay last drawn

q: For a case referred to an empanelled hospital, the key document that names the patient, the ailment, the hospital and the treatment, and against which Accounts checks the hospital bill, is:

options.A: The referral letter
options.B: The UMID card alone
options.C: The pension payment order
options.D: The Fixed Medical Allowance option form

q: Which of the following statements about UMID and RELHS cards is NOT correct?

options.A: The UMID card identifies the beneficiary at any railway hospital or health unit
options.B: The RELHS card, now in UMID form, carries the beneficiary details and the registered hospital
options.C: The UMID card is issued only to RELHS pensioners and not to serving employees or their dependants
options.D: For pensioners, FMA option and RELHS membership are flagged against the beneficiary in the UMID/RELHS record

q: Which of the following statements about checking a medical reimbursement claim in Accounts is NOT correct?

options.A: The sanction of the CMD, with justification recorded, is checked for reimbursement claims
options.B: Reimbursement is a refund of whatever amount was spent, regardless of prescribed rates or ceilings
options.C: Rates in the claim are checked with reference to CGHS rates where so prescribed
options.D: Claims must be supported by original vouchers, prescriptions, discharge summary and the referral or emergency certificate, as applicable

q: Assertion (A): Joining RELHS is optional for a retiring railway employee. Reason (R): The RELHS subscription is recovered at retirement along with the settlement process, on the basis of the option exercised in the settlement papers.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Assertion (A): A pensioner who has opted for Fixed Medical Allowance remains entitled to indoor treatment in a railway hospital. Reason (R): FMA is granted in lieu of the outdoor (OPD) treatment facility only, not in lieu of indoor treatment.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Assertion (A): A serving employee may take treatment in any private hospital of his choice, without referral, and claim reimbursement as of right. Reason (R): Treatment in a recognised or empanelled hospital is admissible on referral by the authorised medical authority, or in a genuine certified emergency.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Match the authority / concept (I-IV) with its role in the railway medical system (a-d): I. Chief Medical Director II. Chief Medical Superintendent III. Authorised Medical Attendant IV. UMID card a. Medical identity document produced for OPD registration, admission and referred treatment b. Head of the medical organisation at the divisional level c. First point of contact - the railway medical officer of the health unit where the beneficiary is registered d. Head of the medical organisation at the zonal level

options.A: I-d, II-c, III-b, IV-a
options.B: I-a, II-b, III-c, IV-d
options.C: I-d, II-b, III-c, IV-a
options.D: I-b, II-d, III-c, IV-a

q: Match the document / check (I-IV) with its function in a medical claim (a-d): I. Referral letter II. Emergency certificate III. Discharge summary IV. CMD sanction a. Records the justification and approval of the competent medical authority for reimbursement b. Certifies that the outside treatment was taken in a genuine emergency c. Names the patient, ailment, hospital and treatment authorised d. Records the treatment actually given during the hospital stay

options.A: I-c, II-d, III-b, IV-a
options.B: I-d, II-b, III-c, IV-a
options.C: I-c, II-b, III-d, IV-a
options.D: I-c, II-b, III-d, IV-b
